investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official /agenda/ page, then its own /agenda/concerts/ ('Musique') category-filtered page discovered via a static <a href> link on that same page. Every event card on both pages is static HTML carrying schema.org microdata attributes (itemprop=name/url, <meta itemprop=startDate>/<meta itemprop=endDate>) directly in the markup — no script execution needed to see any of it.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official agenda page (https://www.gaite-lyrique.net/agenda/) returned 29 static event cards, each carrying schema.org microdata (itemprop=name/url on the title link, <meta itemprop=startDate>/<meta itemprop=endDate>, an itemprop=location Place block for room-level events) directly in the HTML — no JSON-LD, Nuxt/Next payload, or wp-json endpoint was present or needed. The same page also links to a dedicated 'Musique' (/agenda/concerts/) category filter, fetched with the same method and found to expose 15 concert-tagged cards in the identical structured shape. Level 1 fully answered the investigation question; no escalation was needed.

venue_reference: La Gaîté Lyrique (multidisciplinary digital-culture/music venue, 3 bis rue Papin, 75003 Paris)

identity.notes: The retained agenda page's own <title> reads 'Agenda | Gaîté Lyrique' at the venue's own domain gaite-lyrique.net (the task-given official site). No separate address microdata was found on the agenda listing itself, but the domain, branding, and content (Paris cultural/digital-arts programming) are self-consistent with the task-given identity; no third-party domain is involved.

site_classification.platform: Custom CMS (no WordPress/wp-json, Nuxt/__NUXT__, or Next/__NEXT_DATA__ signal detected anywhere in the retained pages). Event cards use schema.org MICRODATA (itemprop attributes) embedded directly in static server-rendered HTML, not JSON-LD script blocks — a different but equally structured, equally parseable pattern.

start_date.notes: Each card's own <meta itemprop=startDate content="2026-09-23T19:30">, stated directly.

time.value: 19:30 (Europe/Paris, floating local — no explicit UTC offset on itemprop=startDate)
time.notes: The same <meta itemprop=startDate> value carries a time-of-day but no timezone offset anywhere on the page — recorded honestly as FLOATING_LOCAL, matching the same certainty model already applied to other sources with unqualified local datetimes (e.g. Badehaus Berlin).

end.notes: Most concert cards' own <meta itemprop=endDate> repeats only the same calendar day as startDate with no time-of-day (e.g. startDate '2026-09-23T19:30', endDate '2026-09-23') — a date-only value, not a genuine performance end-time, the same honest distinction already drawn for Tempodrom Berlin's JSON-LD endDate. One sampled card ('Kiss Facility') does carry a genuine same-day end time (endDate '2026-10-07T23:30'), so this field is not uniformly NOT_PRESENT across the source — recorded PARTIAL rather than either extreme.

venue_location.value: La Gaîté Lyrique, 3 bis rue Papin, 75003 Paris
venue_location.notes: This is a single-venue source: the entire retained page is this venue's own official agenda, and every listed event is this venue's own programme (the same 'resolve by source_id, not per-card restatement' judgement already documented for Badehaus Berlin/ingestion/badehaus/observation-adapter.mjs). Several cards additionally carry a per-room itemprop=location Place (e.g. 'Grande Salle', 'Grande galerie') naming a specific room WITHIN this same venue — retained as supplementary detail, not a different venue.

source_record_id.notes: No numeric ID is exposed on the card; each event's own itemprop=url link is this source's own permanent '/agenda/2026/{slug}/' page, so the slug is used as source_record_id — the same documented judgement already established for moog-barcelona-01/LAV, tempodrom-berlin-01, and truskel-paris-01.

event_url.notes: Each card's own itemprop=url attribute on the title <a>, stated directly as an absolute URL.

price.notes: No price/tarif/€ text was found on any sampled concert card on the listing page itself; a per-event detail page fetch (wolfang-voigt-1) also showed none in the retained excerpt. Not ruled out on other individual event pages not sampled, but honestly NOT_PRESENT on this source's own list-page data path.

reasons: Identity established at HIGH confidence from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, official domain, content).
acquisition_class STATIC_HTML (schema.org microdata cards), a resolved supported class, reached at Level 1 with no escalation needed.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained: the venue's own /agenda/concerts/ ('Musique') category filter, exposing 15 concert cards directly in static HTML.
title, start_date, time, venue_location, source_record_id, and event_url all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.

end is honestly PARTIAL (most cards' endDate encodes only a calendar day, not a real end-time; one sampled card is a genuine exception) and price is honestly NOT_PRESENT on this data path — neither fabricated.

No existing collector family in this repository parses schema.org MICRODATA (itemprop attributes) directly embedded in static HTML — every existing family targets JSON-LD, ICS, RSS, or a JSON/REST API. recommended_family is therefore NEW_FAMILY_REQUIRED, distinct from (but structurally similar in spirit to) the existing JSON-LD family.

No unresolved CRITICAL blocker. READY_FOR_ACTIVATION was deliberately not claimed; turning this into an enabled source is a separate, later, explicitly-authorised step outside this investigation's scope.
